The edition's own statement of rights (from eBible.org's page for this translation, https://ebible.org/latVUC/copyright.htm):
> Clementine Vulgate of 1598 with Glossa Ordinaria Migne edition 1880 in Latin
> Public Domain
> Language: Latine (Latin)
> Translation by: Jerome
> 2014-08-23

Why this is public domain:
Text: the Clementine Vulgate (Rome, 1598) with the Glossa Ordinaria from Migne's Patrologia Latina, volumes 113-114 (Paris, about 1880). People: Jerome (died 420); Robert Bellarmine (1542-1621) and the other Clementine editors of the 1590s; the school of Anselm of Laon (died 1117) for the Glossa; Jacques Paul Migne (1800-1875). US: published before 1931. Origin: Rome (Vatican City, life plus 70 years) and France (life plus 70 years); every named person died before 1876. The digital transcription is unnamed; copying a text adds no author.

The read-aloud archive holds the Bible text chapter by chapter as plain text, a front file, the copyright page (copr.htm, left out of the source), and eBible.org's signing key (keys.asc, left out).

Sources of these facts: eBible.org's details page (https://ebible.org/details.php?id=latVUC), the edition's copyright page (https://ebible.org/latVUC/copyright.htm), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixto-Clementine_Vulgate; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossa_Ordinaria; English Wikipedia pages of Jerome, Bellarmine and Migne; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries%27_copyright_lengths; https://copyright.cornell.edu/publicdomain.

held_out_by.note: eBible's chapter files, <code>_<NNN>_<BOOK>_<CC>_read.txt, are held out by book and chapter, so the same chapter is held out in every translation at once (maintainer's decision, 2026-10-23)

note: eBible.org rebuilds this zip often; the checksum covers the files inside, so a rebuild with the same text still matches.
